source.title: Distributional Spectral Diagnostics for Localizing Grokking Transitions
source.authors: Zi-Yue Wang; Yufeng Ying; T. Kanamori

record.tranche_reason: The study trains models on modular addition and reports training/test accuracy and generalization onset, using the original task/codebase with changed settings.
record.gate_note: The paper's own modular-addition accuracy and onset results bear on V1; its weight-decay/onset comparisons also bear on the tested timing association in V5. Circuit, optimizer-artifact, and large-model claims are not tested. The paper cites mechanistic progress measures and reports CIFAR-10 only as a portability check, explicitly not a grokking benchmark. Auxiliary detector, DMD, and perturbation results do not directly measure the behaviors named by the claim versions.
record.test_reason: The paper is mainly a grokking-detector paper, but it also reports its own modular-addition (mod 97) results on train/test accuracy and onset. It uses Power et al.'s codebase at training fraction 0.4. These results bear on V1: overfitting followed by rapid generalization at wd=1, no delay at wd=2, and non-generalization within 6000 steps at wd=0 and in some architecture cells. The residual-detector results do not measure a behaviour named by any version. The weight-decay timing effect does not test V5's efficiency mechanism, critical size or ungrokking.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors position the residual as a window-level localization and fragility-monitoring signal in the studied modular-arithmetic Transformer settings, not a universal early-warning predictor or an intervention rule. They state norm signals are stronger run-level regime indicators. They report higher weight decay associated with earlier onset as a descriptive scope check, with architecture-dependent strength, and make no circuit-efficiency claim.
record.recipe_differences: Uses the modular-addition task and open-source implementation introduced by Power et al.; changes the training fraction to 0.4 and focuses on distributional spectral diagnostics and weight-decay/architecture checks rather than a direct reproduction protocol.
record.method_sensitivity: Generalization timing varies with weight decay and architecture; residual results also vary with model scale and segment size. The main training fraction is fixed at 0.4.

fits_no_version.finding: Higher weight decay gives earlier 99% onset (wd=1: 3398±361 steps; wd=2: 1528). wd=0 does not generalize within 6000 steps. The ordering holds over a 5-value sweep (App. E) and across segment sizes.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Weight decay strength shortens grokking delay on modular addition, down to no visible delay at high values.

fits_no_version.finding: A DMD reconstruction residual of the correct-answer log-prob distribution rises before test-accuracy onset on held-out runs. AUROC ≈0.93; TPR 0.80 at FPR 0.50; median lead 1068 steps on true-positive alarms. On a reused-seed split it fires no alarms. Norm signals reach run-level AUROC ≈0.98–0.99.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Output-distribution dynamics carry a pre-onset signal of the grokking transition (related to, but not, V2's circuit progress measures).

record.problems: The core pool is small, and the held-out detector evaluation uses 5 grokking and 12 non-grokking runs. Architecture-cell results aggregate only 2 or 5 seeds. Test-accuracy aggregation and onset can diverge in under-generalizing cells; the paper itself notes architecture dependence. The study does not test the training-set-size delay relationship.
record.rows_left_out: No rows for cited circuit/mechanism findings or CIFAR-10 portability: these are not own results on the claimed grokking behavior. Auxiliary residual-detection scores, perturbation sensitivity, norm baselines, and FCN spectral descriptors do not measure a behavior named by the versions. Appendix S mentions fraction/prime sweeps qualitatively but supplies no per-condition numeric result in the text provided.

untested.parts: Delay growing as the training set shrinks (fraction fixed at 0.4; the App. S fraction sweep is qualitative and concerns detector transfer only). No numeric chance-level start.
All: no circuit or mechanistic progress measures. The residual is a detector signal, not a circuit measure.
All: CIFAR-10 and MNIST runs have no grokking transition; initialization scale is not varied.
Efficiency-of-circuit mechanism, critical dataset size, ungrokking.
All; softmax-collapse and slingshot accounts are only cited.

missing.what: Extended weight-decay sweep (wd 0, 0.25, 0.5, 1, 2; 4 seeds each) showing onset shifting earlier with higher wd; figures only, no numbers in text
Train vs test accuracy trajectories showing train accuracy saturating early before the test jump in the representative wd=1 run

record.verdict_notes: Grokking results here are setup and scope checks for a detector paper, so the evidence on V1 is thin: one 6000-step window and fraction fixed at 0.4. All reader links to V5 were removed, because the weight-decay timing effect does not test the efficiency account, critical dataset size or ungrokking. Internal inconsistencies to flag: seed counts (Table 6: 10; Table 7: 8/2/5; §3.3 and App. F: 2 per scale; App. M: 9 wd=1 runs). Table 7 also reports onsets for cells whose mean test accuracy is far below the caption's 99% criterion.

versions.untested_parts: The main experiment fixes the training fraction at 0.4; the paper does not establish that smaller training sets require more optimization. It does not report a numeric chance-level test-accuracy baseline.
The study compares weight decay with generalization timing, but does not test whether this favors a more efficient circuit, identify a critical dataset size, or test ungrokking below such a size.

relationships.reason: Overfitting followed by rapid generalization; test accuracy 0.999 with mean onset 3398 steps (r1, r3).
relationships.display_finding: Rapid generalization followed overfitting, reaching test accuracy 0.999 with a mean onset of 3,398 steps.

relationships.reason: Generalizes early (onset 1528) without a pronounced overfitting period, so the delay depends on weight decay strength (r4).

relationships.reason: Prolonged overfitting, but generalization is described as slow and not reached within 6000 steps (test 0.325); some seeds need >5×10^5 steps (r2).

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.reason: The baseline wd=1 setting has later onset than wd=2, while the no-weight-decay runs can remain overfit far longer; this supports an association between weight decay and earlier generalization, not the proposed circuit-efficiency mechanism; see r2–r4 and r11.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.reason: The weight-decay/generalization relationship is architecture-dependent, with incomplete accuracy or failures to generalize in tested cells; see r5–r10.
